name: bdflush
description: The bdflush system call starts, flushes, or tunes the buffer-dirty-flush daemon. It is deprecated since Linux 2.6 and performs no action, with its functionality handled by kernel threads. Only processes with the CAP_SYS_ADMIN capability can call it.

parameters.name: func
parameters.description: Determines the action: negative or 0 to start the daemon, 1 to flush buffers, even values >=2 for reading parameters, odd values >=3 for setting parameters

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: Pointer to a long word for reading tuning parameters when func is even and >=2

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: Long word value for setting tuning parameters when func is odd and >=3

return_value.success: Returns 0 on success; never returns if starting the daemon successfully
return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error and sets errno

errors.description: An attempt was made to enter the daemon code after another process has already entered
address points outside your accessible address space
An attempt was made to read or write an invalid parameter number, or to write an invalid value to a parameter
Caller does not have the CAP_SYS_ADMIN capability

versions: Deprecated since Linux 2.6; glibc support removed in 2.23
